question: In which of the following plants is the body NOT differentiated into roots, stems and leaves?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chara** is a genus of green algae in the family Characeae.
 
• Unlike higher plants, Chara does not have a body differentiated into roots, stems, and leaves.
 
• Chara has a simple body structure consisting of a thallus without true roots, stems, or leaves.
 
• These algae are found in fresh water and are often referred to as stoneworts due to their calcified structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deodar**

 
 
• Also known as Cedrus deodara, it is a species of cedar native to the western Himalayas.
 
• Deodar trees have a well-differentiated body with roots, stems, and leaves.
 
• They are large evergreen coniferous trees with needle-like leaves.
 
 
 
• **Fern**
 
 
• Ferns are a group of vascular plants that reproduce via spores and have neither seeds nor flowers.
 
• They have a well-differentiated body into roots, stems, and leaves.
 
• Ferns are known for their large, divided leaves called fronds.
 
 
 
• **Marsilea**
 
 
• Marsilea is a genus of aquatic ferns known as water clover.
 
• These plants have a differentiated body with roots, stems, and leaves.
 
• The leaves are typically four-lobed and resemble a clover.
